cls: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) - carbocyclic guanosine analogue
quick: 600 mg once daily or 300 mg twice daily (with other antiretrovirals)
May be taken with or without food
Used in pregnancy when indicated; an alternative NRTI option
Breastfeeding not recommended in HIV (US); avoid
No dose adjustment needed in renal impairment
Reduce dose in mild impairment; avoid in moderate-severe
Alcohol raises abacavir levels (~41%); use caution
HLA-B*5701 before start, hypersensitivity signs, LFTs
summary: Abacavir is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used in combination with other antiretrovirals to treat HIV-1 infection. It carries a BOXED WARNING for serious and potentially fatal hypersensitivity reactions strongly linked to the HLA-B*5701 allele - all patients must be screened for HLA-B*5701 before starting, and the drug must never be restarted after a suspected hypersensitivity reaction. NRTIs as a class carry a boxed warning for lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis. Abacavir has also been associated with increased cardiovascular (myocardial infarction) risk in some studies.
indications: Treatment of HIV-1 infection in combination with other antiretroviral agents

dosage.d: 600 mg once daily OR 300 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Always combined with other antiretrovirals; only after HLA-B*5701 testing

dosage.d: 8 mg/kg twice daily (max 300 mg/dose) or weight-band tablets
dosage.t: Twice daily (or once daily per weight bands)
dosage.n: Use oral solution or scored tablets per weight
Use the 10 mg/mL oral solution to allow the reduced dose

admin: Confirm a NEGATIVE HLA-B*5701 result before the first dose - do not start in HLA-B*5701-positive patients
Counsel the patient on hypersensitivity symptoms and provide a warning/alert card
NEVER rechallenge after a suspected hypersensitivity reaction - re-exposure can cause life-threatening hypotension and death within hours
Always use as part of a combination antiretroviral regimen
moa: Abacavir is a carbocyclic synthetic nucleoside analogue. It is intracellularly converted by cellular enzymes to its active metabolite carbovir triphosphate, an analogue of guanosine triphosphate. Carbovir triphosphate competes with natural dGTP and is incorporated into viral DNA by HIV-1 reverse transcriptase, terminating the DNA chain (lacking the 3'-OH needed for elongation) and thereby inhibiting viral replication.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to abacavir or any component
relative: Risk factors for coronary heart disease
Risk factors for lactic acidosis/hepatic steatosis (obesity, prolonged NRTI use, female)
monitor: Liver function and signs of lactic acidosis

preg: Abacavir may be used during pregnancy when indicated and is an acceptable NRTI component of antiretroviral regimens. The Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry has not detected an increased risk of birth defects; treating maternal HIV reduces vertical transmission. HLA-B*5701 testing still applies.
lact: In settings such as the United States where formula feeding is safe and available, women with HIV are advised not to breastfeed to avoid postnatal HIV transmission. Abacavir is excreted in milk; breastfeeding is not recommended.
renal: No dose adjustment is necessary in renal impairment, as abacavir is primarily metabolized by the liver and is not significantly renally cleared. (Fixed-dose combinations containing renally cleared NRTIs may still require adjustment.)
hepatic: Reduce the dose to 200 mg twice daily (using oral solution) in mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A). Abacavir is CONTRAINDICATED in moderate to severe hepatic impairment because its safe use has not been established.

major: Methadone (abacavir increases methadone clearance - may require methadone dose adjustment)
moderate: Other NRTIs / antiretrovirals causing additive mitochondrial toxicity
minor: Drugs metabolized by UGT/alcohol dehydrogenase pathways
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food (no clinically significant food effect)
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol increases abacavir exposure by about 41%; abacavir does not affect alcohol levels - use with caution
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate liver enzymes, triglycerides, CPK and lactate; monitor as indicated

serious: Hypersensitivity reaction (fever, rash, GI symptoms, respiratory/constitutional symptoms) - potentially fatal, linked to HLA-B*5701
Lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis (class effect)
Possible increased risk of myocardial infarction
Hepatotoxicity / hepatic decompensation (especially with hepatitis co-infection)
emergency: Life-threatening hypersensitivity reaction (hypotension/anaphylaxis-like), especially on rechallenge
Lactic acidosis (deep breathing, vomiting, abdominal pain)

monitoring: HLA-B*5701 genotype before initiating therapy (do not start if positive)
Hypersensitivity symptoms, especially in the first 6 weeks
Liver function tests and signs of lactic acidosis
HIV viral load and CD4 count for efficacy
Cardiovascular risk assessment; lipids and glucose
counsel: You must be tested for the HLA-B*5701 gene before starting; do not start if you carry it
Carry the warning card; learn the symptoms of a hypersensitivity reaction (fever, rash, severe tiredness, GI or breathing symptoms)
If a hypersensitivity reaction is suspected, stop the drug and seek care immediately and NEVER take abacavir again - rechallenge can be fatal
Take exactly as prescribed with your other HIV medicines; do not miss doses (resistance risk)
Limit alcohol, which raises drug levels
Report unusual muscle pain, deep rapid breathing, abdominal pain, or yellowing of skin/eyes
pk: Antiviral activity follows intracellular conversion to active carbovir triphosphate
Plasma peak approximately 0.7-1.5 hours after an oral dose
Plasma half-life ~1.5 hours; intracellular carbovir triphosphate half-life is long, allowing once-daily dosing
Prolonged intracellular activity supports once-daily regimens
Store at 20-25 C; oral solution may be refrigerated but not frozen
pearls: BOXED WARNING: serious/fatal hypersensitivity reactions linked to HLA-B*5701 - screen ALL patients before starting and never rechallenge after a suspected reaction
BOXED WARNING (NRTI class): lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis
No renal dose adjustment needed (hepatically metabolized via alcohol dehydrogenase and glucuronyl transferase)
Contraindicated in moderate-severe hepatic impairment; dose-reduce in mild impairment
Associated with increased myocardial infarction risk in some cohort studies - weigh in patients with cardiac risk
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered, then resume the regular schedule; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose - do not double up. Consistent adherence is critical to prevent HIV resistance. If doses have been interrupted, do NOT restart without medical advice because of hypersensitivity rechallenge risk.
overdose: There is limited experience with abacavir overdose; no specific symptoms or signs have been identified beyond those listed as adverse effects, and no antidote exists. Management is supportive with monitoring and standard care. It is not known whether abacavir is removed by peritoneal dialysis or hemodialysis.
